page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A1.160 is a bare metal server powered by the Arm64 architecture, featuring Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz. The platform delivers 160 physical cores and 160 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core, removing hyperthreading contention. It is provisioned with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 6.4 GB of RAM per physical core. The hardware configuration contains zero GPUs and includes no local storage drives, requiring reliance on remote block or network storage solutions. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark outcomes show high multi-core scaling alongside average to weak single-thread performance. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU performance places in the top 10% with a score of 277,642.0, whereas single-core performance settles in the middle 50% at 1,786.39. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 761.51 GB/sec, placing in the top tier, contrasting sharply with single-threaded compression and decompression figures that fall in the bottom 25%. LLM prompt processing on a 135M parameter model registers 111.1 tokens/sec, falling into the bottom 10%, reflecting the lack of x86-specific advanced matrix extensions or dedicated AI accelerators.

The memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput across various operations, reaching 11,234.81 GB/sec on cached read benchmarks and 367.22 GB/sec on uncached 256MB reads, both landing in the top 10%. Write performance on large blocks achieves 157.46 GB/sec in the top 25%. In operational benchmarks, the instance yields top-tier performance for in-memory structures, clocking 172.16 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, as well as 63.87 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

This server provides strong cost efficiency per core for horizontally scaled, highly threaded applications due to its dense 160-core design and extensive memory footprint. It is well-fitted for memory-intensive caching layers, containerized microservice clusters, distributed data processing, and high-concurrency web serving, while workloads constrained by single-thread latency or requiring local NVMe storage will face trade-offs.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A1.160 is an Arm64 bare metal server featuring 160 dedicated Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 physical cores running at 3.0 GHz and 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory. Operating without hyperthreading or bundled GPUs, the machine relies entirely on network-attached storage since no local disks are included. Performance testing demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution (277,642.0 in multi-core stress-ng) and high memory throughput (367.22 GB/sec on uncached reads), paired with top-tier Redis SET processing of 172.16 million operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks and LLM prompt processing exhibit lower relative performance. Offering 6.4 GB of RAM per dedicated core, BM.Standard.A1.160 serves high-density container orchestration, large in-memory key-value caching, and highly parallelized web server workloads.
